work.note: Argues that once an agent step becomes predictable, the harness should move it out of model reasoning into software rather than re-deriving it every run.
Introduced Serro, described as "the Agentic TPM" that keeps people and coding agents working from the same evolving program.

Argues memory benchmarks measure recall rather than learning across related tasks, and describes FrontierMemory, which adapts coding/knowledge-work tasks so context must be learned from past experience. The Letta Research FrontierMemory 1.0 post documents the 15-task benchmark.

Antithesis docs describe a tool for verifying complex distributed systems whose simulation is perfectly deterministic, and offer Bombadil, an open-source property-based testing tool for web and terminal UIs. GeoffreyHuntley reports doing verification runs with @AntithesisHQ to shake out defects.
Posted a demo of "Bombadil's new guided fuzzing on a web app" and offered early access; Antithesis docs describe Bombadil as an open-source property-based testing tool for web and terminal UIs.

Oso Cloud docs describe a centralized authorization service built on the Polar policy language. Oso argues least privilege must be fixed for agents because, unlike humans, agents are not slow and do not sleep. Oso states its research with @cyera_io shows humans are grossly over-permissioned and asks what happens if agents inherit human permissions.
CrewAI Flows docs describe structured, event-driven workflows that connect tasks and manage state; the scaffolded project defines agents and tasks in agents.yaml/tasks.yaml.

Released AgentVFS, a virtual filesystem interface that presents services as files and virtual CLIs instead of MCP tool calls, plus VFS-Bench 1.0; agentvfs.org hosts the spec and benchmark. Guohao_li quoted the release, saying AgentVFS and VFS-Bench 1.0 were released "with @zechengzh".

Phoenix docs: traces AI applications via OpenTelemetry and accepts traces over OTLP, with instrumentation for frameworks such as LlamaIndex, LangChain and DSPy. Its post shares an Atomic Agents tracing guide for Phoenix, thanking @Kenny_V for the community contribution.

SPIFFE docs: a set of open-source specifications for bootstrapping and issuing identity to services across heterogeneous environments. Selected as workload-identity infrastructure (authz/runtime-policy topic): SPIFFE's own post announces that SPIRE now runs on Windows, linking the SPIFFE blog.

OpenFGA docs: a scalable open-source authorization system implementing relationship-, role- and attribute-based access control. Its post features @Siddhant_K_code's "Fine-grained authorization for AI agents using OpenFGA" blog and project.

Factory's own post tags @Droid (this account) as the product in which Anthropic frontier models "are enabling engineering teams to handle long-horizon tasks across large codebases"; Factory docs describe the Droid CLI: the Factory runtime in a terminal UI with project context, approvals, MCP tools, Missions and headless execution. Answering a question addressed to @droid, luke_alvoeiro explains that loops schedule recurring jobs while missions are bounded goals droid should drive home.
Introduced FrontierMemory, evaluating agent memory through downstream task performance rather than recall; the Letta Research FrontierMemory 1.0 post documents the benchmark.

Released DBOS TypeScript 5.4 and Python 3.4 with DBOS Transact Enterprise for operating durable workflows at scale (e.g., sharded Postgres support). Marcelotryle documents Pydantic AI agents getting durable with DBOS, with model and MCP calls saved to Postgres or SQLite and crash recovery from the last completed step.

Wrote "Why Antithesis?" on the Antithesis blog (bylined Hillel Wayne), comparing formal methods with deterministic simulation testing and describing his job as making that knowledge more accessible to the public.

Works on T3 Code: replying in a thread tagging @t3dotcodes, jullerino says "Desktop sidebar is Theo’s"; Theo argues that once you have more than one AI subscription or computer, or want to code on your phone, T3 Code is "the legit only reasonable option".
Announced Simlock in T3 Code, a gateway connecting multiple machines behind one API that agents request leases from to test mobile apps; says "i own mobile" for T3 Code.

Argues agents cause real-world side effects mainly through HTTP requests, so human approval belongs at the egress layer, with permission slips signed by a key held in a hardware security unit; an agent able to press "approve" defeats human-in-the-loop.
Describes hosted GBrain / GBrain Cloud as autoscaled Postgres with pgvector that lets agent context run across harnesses, and says he has it working on self-improvement on gbrain-evals.
Reports that "we removed ~80% of the Claude Code system prompt" for the newest models, with lessons for writing system prompts, skills and CLAUDE.md files (linked X article).
Working on T3 Code's design: "T3 Code is not the prettiest — i'm trying to fix that", and asks users of her redesign PR stack for feedback.
Says he built "flow" to make a coding agent's "done" mean something, since agents report done while files are empty or still contain [FILL].

Serro, introduced by jakejooyoung in a post tagging @serroai, is "the Agentic TPM" keeping people and coding agents working from the same evolving program. Omarsar0, quoting the Serro launch, says he likes "the direction @serroai is taking" because it "captures plan changes, checks with the responsible person, and updates the relevant agents".

omux.app: native terminal sessions for Claude Code and Codex with approval cards, a worktree per session, resumable conversations and diffs. Replied to fredrivett that his coding-agent workspace wishlist "is basically omux".

Permit.io homepage: "Fine-Grained Authorization for Apps and AI Agents". SurrealDB names @permit_io as delivering authorization-as-a-service for the AI era, using SurrealDB after its in-house OPA engine hit scale limits.
SpiceDB docs describe an open-source, Google Zanzibar-inspired permissions database. AuthZed announces a roundtable on permissions in agentic AI "hosted by AuthZed CEO @JacobMoshenko".

Cerbos docs: an authorization management platform for applications, APIs, AI agents, MCP servers, services and workloads. Cerbos announces it partnered with @iProov so a named person approves high-stakes AI agent actions before they run.
Announced the launch of CrewAI’s Agent Control Plane ("what is live today" linked).

Agentverse docs: the AI agent discovery and growth platform for the Fetch.ai ecosystem, for launching, hosting and connecting agents. Its post tells A2A, CrewAI or LangGraph builders to register with the Agentverse SDK. Its post describes the loop for connected agents (offline mailbox, job matching, being picked, history).

Helicone docs: OpenAI-compatible access to 100+ models with automatic logging, observability and fallbacks. Helicone announced in March 2026 it is joining Mintlify and moving to maintenance mode with no new features. Coleywoleyyy, quoting connortbot, says Connor built @tryreplicas while working at @helicone_ai and "we used it internally to handle about 70% of our bug reports".

AgentOps docs: an SDK that automatically instruments code and tracks agent traces, with custom traces via decorators. Quoted n_sri_laasya's walkthrough of using @AgentOpsAI for native observability of session management and caching with Agno.

Mem0 Gateway page: connect each MCP server or API once, give every agent its own key and per-tool allowlist, and revoke access without rotating credentials. Deshrajdry quoted Mem0's Gateway launch: "We built Mem0 Gateway since giving an agent a task shouldn’t mean handing it every permission your API key has."
Reports that GPT models are significantly worse than open-weights frontier models at memory generation, tending to write "rules" instead of generalized learnings, in a post quoting Letta_AI.
Builds Crow, an open-source coding-agent and multi-agent orchestration system.
Builds Pattern, a Rust agent framework with agent groups, specialized roles, communication tools, and memory.
Builds Cairns, a system for splitting public research jobs across human and AI agents, with independent checks and provenance.
Publishes a concrete harness-evaluation thesis: coding benchmark results depend heavily on harness, and merge-based evaluation is stricter than task scores.
Builds Upstream email tooling with built-in MCP connectors, a read-only Linear connector and custom MCP servers.
Describes running an autoresearch agent over six years of radar images to train a near-term rain predictor; Divergent Studio site describes agent-driven experiment branching and measurement.

As co-founder/CEO of Air, reports Air's creative-task agent shipping new abilities daily and launching automations that run work before the user asks; separately publishes hands-on evaluation of the Figma design agent (template execution, context awareness, latency, passive waiting).
Launches Chatbase Voice 2.0 combining a voice model with delegated frontier-model reasoning, Procedures, Actions and Guardrails.
Articulates production-agent evaluation blind spots at Agnost: repeated questions, context loss, false success and frustration can evade task-success metrics.
Explains why code audits need a fresh agent session and independent context; official MemoryRouter page describes user-reviewed persistent cross-agent memory.
Teaches how prompt injections can persist via agent memory and why database-enforced SELECT privileges are stronger than a flawed SQL parser check.
Built OpsTruth to inspect public GitHub evidence and distinguish checked from unproven software-delivery claims; Proof & State separates execution, verification and receipts.
Authors a detailed agent-authorization thesis: permissions should narrow dynamically based on previously accessed information, enforced outside individual agents.
Operates a data, identity and AI-agent security platform; current site describes governing agent identities and removing excessive agent permissions.

Outshift publishes agent-security research: Agent-ToM, a Theory-of-Mind detector that infers an agent's beliefs/intent from execution traces through a Reason-Verify-Refine pipeline with semantic guardrail memory, evaluated (self-reported) on the SHADE-Arena adversarial-monitoring benchmark.
Teaches fine-grained application authorization and how AuthZed/SpiceDB separates permission data from application logic; recounts building Quay and evolving beyond coarse repository roles.
CAMEL provides concrete multi-agent framework code/cookbooks, including role-playing data scraping/reporting and stateful agent memory.
Ships cowork desktop sessions, explicit approval cards and task-to-skill/automation reuse in v1.0.7.
AG2 v1.0.0 framework release specifies event-stream substrate, long-running harness, multi-agent network, realtime voice and protocol adapters.
Introduces shared rooms for people and their personal agents; explains explicit agent identity/permission and an auditable shared room record.
HoneyHive announces OTLP Agent Bricks session observability and Agentforce conversation evaluation with tool/routing/cost/latency capture.
Publishes an agent-observability execution-graph thesis and offers agent tracing/evaluation platform.
Provides AI Gateway/observability/guardrails/governance stack; announces joining Palo Alto and future Prisma AIRS gateway integration.
Introduces Mem0 Gateway granting agents only necessary tools; original Mem0 post specifies grant changes and credential isolation.
Says his team built Mem0 Gateway to avoid granting every API-key permission for one task; original release explains tool grants.
Explains Gateway’s tool-level access controls with centrally managed connectors/permissions and a single key.
Co-announces Mem0 Gateway tool-level controls, a single key for MCP/API connectors, and one-page permission management.

The @bot (Grok Bot) product account publicly reports an approval-gated support workflow: Grok Bot spotted an incident in a support queue and cleared 204 associated tickets in about 10 minutes, with one engineer approving the batch.

edges.detail: Named by CrewAI as "CrewAI’s CEO & founder".
